sources.classification: labelled from the task code, 2026-10-10: a transformer language model trained from scratch, so `ai_training`; precision fp16 (autocast and gradient scaler); params counted from the layer shapes = 191 948 759 = embedding 137 080 320 (267 735 tokens x 512, tied with the output weights) + output bias 267 735 + 16 layers x 3 412 480 + relative-position biases 1 024 (vocabulary 267 735: WikiText-103 training tokens and <eos>, not counted on the stand's machine); seq_len = target length (the memory adds 192 more positions of context); the run is bounded by max_step 400, not by epochs: epochs and dataset_samples are left out

measurements.source: Lambda, github.com/lambdal/deeplearning-benchmark, commit aa5addb6 (2025-12-17), pytorch/pytorch-train-throughput-fp16.csv, column transformerxlbase (training throughput, tokens/s), single-GPU rows run with batch 104 (pytorch/pytorch-train-bs-fp16.csv; config_pytorch_80GB.sh): 'A100 80GB SXM4' 43078; 'A100 80GB PCIe' 41602; 'H100 80GB PCIe Gen5' 47919, 'LambdaCloud H100 80GB PCIe Gen5' 45433; 'H100 80GB SXM5' 62259 (the five other H100 80GB SXM5 rows hold 0.0 and are left out)
measurements.date: measurement dates are not in the CSV; repository snapshot 2025-12-17
measurements.hardware: Lambda's systems as named in the rows; NVIDIA NGC PyTorch container (version not recorded per row), LambdaLabsML/DeepLearningExamples branch lambda/benchmark; fp16 through APEX AMP O2 (the task file uses torch.cuda.amp: see its docstring)

measurements.compute_ratio_note: throughput[A100 80GB SXM4] / throughput[GPU]; the two H100 PCIe rows pooled by geometric mean (46659 tokens/s); H100 SXM5 is one host. The throughput is tokens / elapsed time per 10 steps, averaged over 400 steps after the first 3 values
